newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Portuguese "secrets" on East Timor to be published.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese "secrets" on East Timor to be published.

text.p: A Portuguese businessman who supports the integration of East Timor with Indonesia said on Saturday he planned to publish a book revealing a number of "secrets" about Lisbon's relationship with its former colony.

"During the last four years I have collected a number of documents in Portugal which are very secret," Manuel Macedo, president of the Portugal-Indonesia Friendship Association, told a news conference.

"I plan to publish these in a book called "The Secret Documents of East Timor," Macedo said, adding it was part of his efforts to persuade the Portuguese government and people to recognise Indonesia's annexation of East Timor.

Mecado, on a one-week business trip to Indonesia, declined to say what he would reveal before the book's publication in May but said it would show there is no need for a referendum to decide the disputed territory's future.

Jakarta invaded East Timor in December 1975 after Lisbon abandoned its colony, and unilaterally declared the territory its 27th province in July the following year. The United Nations still regards Portugal as East Timor's administering power.
